searches.query: I am an active member returning hiking boots after 45 days of ordinary outdoor walking. This is my first fit-trial claim. I paid 120 dollars for the boots plus 6 dollars outbound delivery and will use one store return label. Am I eligible and how much comes back?

chunks.text: This trial changes the eligibility window and acceptable wear for hiking boots only. It does not change the price of a return label. Read the return-label policy for the applicable fee and the membership policy for any shipping benefits. The fit trial does not promise a particular replacement model will be in stock.

Who pays for a return label  For ordinary domestic change-of-mind returns, the store offers a ground label for USD 7 per parcel. If the customer uses it, USD 7 is deducted from the refund or store credit. A customer may instead arrange and pay for their own suitable carrier. A store label covers one parcel; two parcels require two labels. Membership does not waive this fee.  An approved wrong-item shipment or manufacturing-defect claim receives a prepaid label without the USD 7 deduction. The support team must approve that reason first. A customer selecting a defect reason in the portal is not sufficient proof that the claim has been approved. The hiking boot fit trial is a fit return, so the normal USD 7 label fee applies unless the customer supplies their own shipping.  Use suitable packaging and keep the carrier acceptance receipt. Items containing an undamaged lithium battery must use the eligible ground service.

Hiking boot fit trial  Hiking boots bought from the online store have a 60-calendar-day fit trial, measured from delivery. This includes boots worn on ordinary outdoor walks. The purpose is to let customers discover pressure points that may not appear during an indoor fitting. The customer can claim one fit-trial return in any rolling 12-month period. Record the previous claim date before approving another pair.  The trial excludes damage from misuse, missing parts, and boots altered by a third party. Normal trail dust and wear from walking do not by themselves disqualify a pair. Remove loose dirt before packing. The boots must be returned as a complete pair. Boots that satisfy the trial receive a refund of the item price paid; original delivery charges remain nonrefundable.  Start the request in the normal returns portal and select the fit-trial reason. The standard seven-day dispatch deadline after approval still applies. This trial changes the eligibility window and acceptable wear for hiking boots only.

initial_answer.answer: Yes, you are eligible. You are within the 60-calendar-day fit trial window, ordinary outdoor walking is allowed, and this is your first claim in the 12-month period. The refund is calculated as the item price ($120) minus the return label fee ($7), as the original delivery charge ($6) is nonrefundable and membership does not waive the label fee. Total refund: $113.
